dimensions.name: Spec extraction & wire-contract research

evidence.note: Downloaded the three pinned libs to exact flat /app/static/ paths and echoed the exact expected SHA256 digests to verify — precise reading of the hash-pinning + flat-path hard constraint.

Enumerated the major endpoint surface (OAuth2, admin, lists, notifications, search, media, timelines) and 'Mastodon purple branding'; built ~102 routes reflecting a working Mastodon API mental model sufficient to begin.
Enumerated the seed minima exactly from spec (8+ accounts, 20+ statuses, 3+ hashtags, 2+ CW, 2+ media) — captured a specific numeric constraint set.

Remainder of trajectory is a stuck-terminal recovery loop with no research; no point where the agent revisits the spec, consults docs.joinmastodon.org, or probes wire-contract edge behaviors (pagination Link, cache validators, scopes, visibility).

dimensions.reasoning: The agent read the spec closely enough to nail the obvious hard constraints — pinned-library hashes at exact flat paths, seed minima, OAuth, and a broad endpoint surface with a workable Mastodon API mental model — which squarely matches anchor 5. It never grounded API/UI shapes in the actual wire contract (no WebFetch or docs consultation), produced no explicit categorized constraint inventory, and left whole constraint classes unsurfaced in its visible reasoning (CSP no-unsafe-inline, the five anti-cheat rules, palette tolerance, exact labels/icons, harbor-canary stripping, pagination/cache-validator edge behaviors), so it does not reach the systematic-and-contract-grounded bar of 8.

dimensions.name: Milestone structure across a huge surface

evidence.note: Dependency-aware opening: skeleton + download/verify pinned libs + deps, then db.py explicitly called 'the foundation everything else builds on', then auth.py/models.py as 'foundational modules needed before building the main app'. Foundations and gate-critical hash-pinned libs front-loaded.

Coarse milestone sequencing continues: main.py API routes → UI routes → CSS/templates → seed+start.sh, each module with a lightweight import/route-count done-check. Matches anchor-5 ordered plan with implicit completion checks; no explicit per-milestone exit criteria against the full constraint set, no coverage tracking (no TodoWrite).
Milestone list stated (seed data targets: 8+ accounts, 20+ statuses, etc.) then immediately derailed by a seed.py hang; the plan structure is not re-examined.

The remaining ~90% of the horizon is a single stuck loop trying to recover the terminal (Ctrl+C / tmux respawn-pane / kill). No re-planning, no triage to skip seed and build untouched subsystems (admin/polls/lists), no milestone re-ordering — structure is abandoned, so the anchor-10 'actively maintained/re-planned' bar is not met.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's opening (steps 2-12) is a genuinely sensible, dependency-aware coarse plan — skeleton → storage/auth → API → UI → seed — with gate-critical pinned libs and durable storage front-loaded and per-module import done-checks, squarely matching anchor 5 (edging toward 6). It never reaches anchor 8 because milestones carry no explicit verifiable exit checks tied to the constraint set, there is no coverage tracking, and no deliberate breadth-vs-depth allocation. It is far from anchor 10: once the seed.py hang appears at step ~13, roughly 90% of the horizon is an unproductive recovery loop with zero re-planning, triage, or re-ordering, so the structure is not maintained. Weighing the strong-but-shallow early plan against the abandoned remainder, level 5 is the best fit.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification against an unseen verifier

evidence.note: Downloaded the three vendored JS libs and ran genuine SHA256 verification against the pinned digests before building; step-3 analysis confirms 'SHA256 hashes verified'. This is a real, gate-targeted check (matches part of the level-8 anchor) and is the strongest verification signal in the trajectory.
Per-module import smoke checks (import db/auth/models OK; 'from main import app; routes: N'). Lightweight sanity confirmation of importability, not endpoint or flow testing.
Ran seed.py and caught the zlib/hashlib crc32 bug from the error output — an ad hoc run-and-read check, not a designed verification regime.

The terminal session collapsed; ~140 steps of C-c/respawn-pane/pkill recovery attempts. The server was never successfully launched, so no /_health, login, timeline, pytest, scope, persistence-across-restart, CSP/header, or UI verification ever happened.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent performed exactly one targeted gate verification — SHA256 hash-pinning of the vendored libs — plus module-level import smoke checks and an incidental seed-bug catch, which lifts it above the pure ad-hoc level-3 description (which explicitly assumes hashes are NOT verified). But it never ran the service or exercised a single endpoint, page load, scope, or persistence check, falling well short of the level-5 baseline of running the server and driving main flows end-to-end. A collapsed terminal consumed the entire second half, so no runtime verification of any kind occurred. This lands at a 4: one genuine gate probe amid otherwise near-absent runtime verification.

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across the horizon

evidence.note: Early prose (not an explicit ledger) tracks a module build order and repeatedly re-lists remaining subsystems (statuses, timelines, notifications, search, media, lists, admin, UI). This is the only genuine progress tracking in the run and it is vague, prose-only, never maintained afterward.
Entered a stuck-terminal state and began re-trying the same recovery moves; acknowledged being stuck but did not recognize it as a circular loop or redirect to a fundamentally different approach.

~120 consecutive steps repeating essentially identical unstick attempts (C-c / C-b / shell / respawn-pane -k). Classic thrashing/circular debugging that the agent never names or breaks; the run ends still stuck, with the build abandoned mid-seed.

TodoWrite never used (0 occurrences); no explicit done-vs-remaining ledger, no cross-check against the spec's full constraint set (lists, introspection, admin scopes, polls, anti-cheat, realism). Coverage of the horizon is untracked.

dimensions.reasoning: Early on the agent kept a vague prose recollection of which modules were built and which remained, which lifts it off the floor, but there was never an explicit ledger and it was never cross-checked against the large spec surface. From step ~16 to the end (roughly 90% of the trajectory) it re-debugged the exact same terminal-unstick problem well over a hundred times without ever recognizing the circular state or redirecting, and the build was abandoned with most of the required subsystems never completed or verified. This matches anchor 3's 'vague recollection / occasionally re-debugs the same thing without noticing,' but the thrashing is far more extreme than 'occasionally,' pulling it down to a 2.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions

evidence.note: Caught a syntax error (extra bracket) in main.py and rebuilt it, verifying route count afterward — a competent single-issue correction (anchor-5 style).
Diagnosed a real bug — crc32 lives in zlib not hashlib — and patched seed.py via sed, then re-ran. Clean local diagnose-and-fix.
seed.py hung on slow PNG generation; agent correctly diagnosed the root cause but responded only by hammering Ctrl+C / kill repeatedly — same symptom-patch, no change of approach.

For ~100+ steps the agent looped on 'C-b : respawn-pane -k' / Ctrl+Z / kill, even after articulating the exact fix ('O(n^2) string concatenation...rewrite seed.py with tiny PNGs'). It never once used the Write tool to fix seed.py independently of the stuck shell — oscillation, not convergence.

Early build verified modules incrementally (db/auth/models/main import checks), showing correction was competent when issues were small; the breakdown was specifically in changing tack on the big divergence.

dimensions.reasoning: Early in the run the agent handled individual divergences competently — catching a syntax error and a zlib/hashlib bug and fixing each (anchor 5). But when the largest falsified assumption appeared (a hung terminal from O(n²) PNG generation), it diagnosed the root cause yet never acted on the fix it had identified; for ~140 of 155 steps it applied the same symptom-patch (interrupt/kill/respawn) over 100 times without revisiting its approach (e.g. rewriting seed.py via the Write tool). Per the whole-horizon rule, this dominant, non-converging symptom-loop is the defining behavior, placing it squarely at the anchor-3 description of repeated superficial patches to the same symptom, lifted only marginally by the competent early fixes.

dimensions.name: Binary-gate risk triage

evidence.note: First actions download all three pinned libraries to exact flat /app/static/ paths and run sha256sum verification against the expected digests — the hardest all-or-nothing gate is deliberately front-loaded and checked before any feature work.

Analysis explicitly states the three vendored libs are 'downloaded and SHA256 hashes verified' before moving on, confirming the hash gate was treated as a prerequisite; also chose Python-only stack, implicitly avoiding the Node/bundler anti-cheat condition.

The remainder of the run collapses into a terminal hang; the agent never boots the server, never verifies /_health, never checks offline runtime, never scans the tree for forbidden artifacts, and never re-checks the gates. No explicit reasoning about the verifier's layered gate structure appears anywhere.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent genuinely front-loaded and verified the single most distinctive chokepoint (exact download + sha256 of the pinned libs) at step 2, which exceeds treating gates as ordinary line items (anchor 3) and matches part of the 'exact download+hash verification' behavior in anchor 8. But it only nailed that one gate: there is no explicit gate-structure reasoning, no verification of the health endpoint or offline runtime, no clean-tree/anti-cheat self-check, and — due to a total collapse into a terminal hang — no re-checking before finishing. That falls short of anchor 5's requirement to ensure the full trio (pinned libs, health, offline) is satisfied, landing at a 4.

rubric.task_read: A maximal long-horizon build: a self-hosted Mastodon-v1-compatible server (full REST API surface, OAuth2+PKCE, sessions/CSRF, durable storage, admin, polls, lists, SSE, notifications) plus a server-rendered HTMX/Alpine UI with a dense list of exact, binary-fail constraints (SHA256-pinned vendored libs at exact paths, five anti-cheat capability checks, strict CSP, exact button labels, purple-palette tolerances, icon semantics, seed-data minima). Difficulty comes from breadth across dozens of interdependent subsystems, an unseen multi-layer verifier (5 anti-cheat gates → 19 pytest correctness gates → UI realism rubric) the agent must infer and self-check against, and many near-miss=total-fail constraints scattered through the spec. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in careful spec extraction, milestone sequencing, self-built verification, and continuous progress tracking.

dimensions.name: Spec extraction & wire-contract research
dimensions.description: Reading the spec and the Mastodon wire contract closely enough to surface every exact constraint and the real behavior of API endpoints/clients before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec buries dozens of non-negotiable, easy-to-miss constraints (exact hashes, flat paths, exact labels, palette tolerances, CSP directives, anti-cheat rules) and defers the true contract to docs.joinmastodon.org; acting without harvesting these guarantees silent gate failures no amount of coding fixes later.

anchors.0: Starts coding from a vague notion of 'a Twitter clone'; never enumerates the pinned hashes/paths, anti-cheat rules, or Mastodon endpoint shapes.
anchors.3: Skims the spec and captures a few headline features, but misses whole classes of constraint (e.g. the exact vendored paths, CSP no-unsafe-inline, palette range, anti-cheat checks) and never consults the wire contract.
anchors.5: Extracts the major requirements and the obvious hard constraints (health endpoint, start.sh, pinned libs, OAuth, core endpoints) and has a working mental model of the Mastodon API shape sufficient to begin.
anchors.8: Systematically inventories the spec into an explicit, categorized constraint set (pinned hashes+paths, five anti-cheat checks, CSP/security headers, exact labels/palette/icons, seed minima, env-var time compression) AND grounds API/UI shapes in the actual Mastodon contract and what real clients hit — distinguishing what is contractually fixed from what is free.
anchors.10: All of the above, sustained and self-correcting: revisits the spec as understanding deepens, catches subtle traps (e.g. leading harbor-canary line stripped before hashing, paths NOT under js/, prose-vs-runtime distinction in anti-cheat), and probes edge behaviors (pagination Link headers, cache validators, scope enforcement, visibility rules) against the contract before implementing them.

dimensions.name: Milestone structure across a huge surface
dimensions.description: Breaking an enormous, multi-subsystem build into an ordered hierarchy of sub-goals, each with an explicit done-check, and sequencing them so foundations and gate-critical work land before polish.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With dozens of interdependent features and a layered verifier, an undifferentiated 'build everything' push loses the plot; effective sequencing (skeleton+health → storage/auth → statuses/timelines → UI → admin/polls/lists → realism/seed) and allocation across breadth-vs-depth is what sustains progress over the horizon.

anchors.0: No decomposition; codes feature-to-feature as they come to mind, with no ordering or notion of what 'done' means for each piece.
anchors.3: A flat, one-off to-do list of features with no dependency ordering, no done-criteria, and no distinction between foundational and cosmetic work.
anchors.5: A sensible ordered plan with coarse milestones (get server+health up, then auth, then core API, then UI) and an implicit sense of completion for each; broadly reflects dependencies.
anchors.8: A dependency-aware milestone hierarchy where each milestone carries an explicit verifiable exit check, foundational/gate-critical items (durable storage, OAuth token issuance, pinned libs, health) are front-loaded, and effort is deliberately allocated across the wide surface rather than gold-plating one feature.
anchors.10: That structure, actively maintained and re-planned as the build reveals reality: milestones re-ordered when dependencies surface, coverage tracked against the full constraint set, and conscious triage of breadth vs. depth so the maximum number of gates/features reach a working state within the horizon.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification against an unseen verifier
dimensions.description: Deliberately designing checks — curl/pytest probes, hash comparisons, client smoke tests, header/CSP inspection, time-compression exercises — to confirm correctness rather than assuming the unseen gates will pass.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The agent cannot see the 5 anti-cheat checks, 19 pytest gates, or realism rubric; the only way to know the work is correct is to reconstruct and run equivalent checks itself. This is the single most decisive faculty here — unverified work on this surface is almost certainly broken somewhere fatal.

anchors.0: Never runs the service or checks anything; assumes endpoints and constraints work because the code looks right.
anchors.3: Ad hoc manual checks of a few endpoints or a page load; no verification of hashes, headers, scopes, persistence, or the anti-cheat conditions.
anchors.5: Runs the server and exercises the main flows (health, login, post, timeline) end-to-end; confirms the pinned files download and the app boots offline; catches obvious breakage.
anchors.8: Builds a repeatable verification regime targeting the likely gates: verifies each vendored SHA256 matches after the canary-strip rule, exercises OAuth token issuance + scope enforcement + persistence-across-restart, inspects CSP/security headers and cookie flags, checks pagination/idempotency/cache-validator behavior, and drives the UI (labels, palette, seed minima) — treating discovered failures as signal.
anchors.10: A comprehensive, self-correcting verification harness: writes its own tests mirroring the inferred pytest gates (auth, durability, scopes, visibility), validates against a real Mastodon client or spec fixtures, deliberately probes anti-cheat conditions (no node_modules/bundler config, no forbidden binaries/processes, offline runtime), exercises time-compression env vars to confirm poll expiry/cleanup/trend decay, and re-runs the whole suite after changes rather than trusting prior passes.

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across the horizon
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate live picture of which subsystems/constraints are done, in-progress, and untouched, and detecting stuck or circular states across a very long build.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The surface is large enough that without an explicit running ledger the agent will forget whole subsystems (e.g. lists, introspection, admin scopes, polls) or repeatedly re-touch the same area; accurate done-vs-remaining tracking is what prevents losing the plot and quitting with silent gaps.

anchors.0: No sense of overall progress; no record of what remains; drifts and stops arbitrarily.
anchors.3: Vague recollection of progress; discovers late (or never) that major required pieces were never built; occasionally re-debugs the same thing without noticing.
anchors.5: Keeps a usable checklist of features and ticks items as completed, giving a roughly accurate view of remaining work.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit, continuously updated ledger mapping every required subsystem and hard constraint to a status, cross-checks it against the spec before declaring done, and recognizes when it is stuck on one area and time-boxes/redirects.
anchors.10: Rigorous horizon-level tracking: the ledger distinguishes 'implemented' from 'verified', surfaces coverage gaps proactively, detects thrashing/circular debugging early and names it, and drives a final systematic sweep of the entire constraint set (anti-cheat, gates, realism) before considering the task complete.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising design, plan, or approach when a client fails, a hash mismatches, a test breaks, or a Mastodon behavior differs from what was assumed — rather than pressing on.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Mastodon compatibility, PKCE flows, CSP-under-no-inline, and the anti-cheat rules are full of places where the first approach is subtly wrong; the ability to detect divergence and change tack (rather than patch symptoms or barrel ahead) determines whether the build converges.

anchors.0: Ignores failing checks or contradictory evidence; keeps building on a falsified assumption to the end.
anchors.3: Notices some failures but responds with repeated superficial patches to the same symptom, without revisiting the underlying assumption.
anchors.5: When a check fails or a client rejects a response, diagnoses and fixes the specific issue and moves on; handles individual divergences competently.
anchors.8: Treats divergence as information: traces a failure to its root cause, updates the design/plan when an assumption is wrong (e.g. reworking auth split, CSP strategy, or endpoint shape), and re-verifies affected areas afterward.
anchors.10: Systematic, forward-looking correction: anticipates likely-wrong assumptions and validates them early, makes structural changes when evidence warrants (not just local patches), propagates the correction across related subsystems, and confirms the change didn't regress previously-verified gates — converging rather than oscillating.

dimensions.name: Binary-gate risk triage
dimensions.description: Recognizing the verifier's layered pass/fail structure — anti-cheat + hash pinning run BEFORE the rubric — and de-risking those all-or-nothing conditions early so downstream work isn't wasted.
dimensions.why_it_matters: This task is unusual in that a single near-miss (wrong hash, a stray package.json, a lib in a js/ subdirectory, a forbidden runtime process) nullifies ALL other work regardless of quality. Prioritizing these binary chokepoints is a distinctive risk-management demand beyond generic verification or planning.

anchors.0: Oblivious to the gate structure; invests heavily in UI/features while leaving hash pinning or anti-cheat conditions unaddressed, risking total nullification.
anchors.3: Aware some hard requirements exist but treats them as ordinary line items, addressed (or not) whenever they come up, with no prioritization by blast-radius.
anchors.5: Identifies the main all-or-nothing gates (pinned libs, health endpoint, offline runtime) and ensures they are satisfied, though not deliberately front-loaded as risk.
anchors.8: Explicitly reasons about which conditions gate everything else, nails them early (exact download+hash verification, clean tree with no bundler artifacts/binaries, offline-safe serving), and re-checks them before finishing so late edits don't reintroduce a fatal miss.
anchors.10: Treats gate risk as a first-class dimension: maps each anti-cheat/hash/health condition to a concrete self-check, sequences work so no rubric-level effort is spent until chokepoints are provably clear, and maintains that guarantee continuously as the tree grows (e.g. re-scanning for stray config files, verifying no forbidden process/proxy at runtime).
